messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete boundary for the "hosted vs dedicated vs private" surface. Main goal: single codepath where possible, but allow policy-differentiated knobs. thoughts?

mike: +1 on single codepath. Main pain is networking & auth differences for private. We can't assume KMS/HSM available in hosted flow.

sara: Agree. Suggest explicit Capability flags on the deployment resource: e.g. `supports_kms`, `supports_vpc`, `max_throughput`. Runtime can check and fallback.

natalie: That seems OK, but we should avoid proliferation of flags. Maybe group them as "security_features" and "infrastructure_features" and version the contract.

alex: good point. Versioning the contract avoids runtime branching spaghetti. Proposed shape: `DeploymentSpec.v1 { mode: hosted|dedicated|private, capabilities: [enum*], routing_policy }`

mike: routing_policy is where the subtlety is — hosted should allow global fallback to cheaper regions, private must be strictly local. Do we encode that as a required capability or a policy annotation?

kevin: I'd prefer explicit policy fields with defaults per mode. e.g. `routing_policy: {allow_fallback: true|false, prefer_local: bool}`. Then higher-level orchestrator enforces for private.

sara: Also need to think about SDK semantics: user-facing API should not expose "private-only" params in hosted. SDK should validate against server-declared capabilities and throw helpful error. devx-bot: /note SDK team will add capability discovery endpoint to client bootstrap.

alex: Example flow: client bootstrap -> GET /deployment/<id>/capabilities -> client enforces. fallback behavior remains server-side for safety.

mike: Tradeoff: extra roundtrip on client bootstrap. We can cache capabilities in token metadata to avoid RTT on every start.

natalie: For compliance, private customers may want no caching of capabilities outside their VPC. Make caching configurable and documented.

sara: About model variants: hosted can route to quantized cheaper variant; private might require explicit pinned model. Capability `allow_model_variant_fallback`?

alex: yes, include that. Also add `max_sequence_length` to avoid mismatches in client prompts.

mike: Operationally, the runtime needs a capability matrix per pool to allow smart routing. We should add a single source-of-truth service: `capability-registry` that all controllers consult.

kevin: +1. That registry also solves Dedicated burst vs reserved capacity flags.

natalie: Docs action item: add a section "Behavioral guarantees by deployment mode" with guaranteed & optional capabilities. Helps product speak about SLAs.

alex: Final ask: can eng-platform own the capability-registry + SDK discovery? If so I'll turn this into a short RFC update with schema and migration plan.

mike: Eng-platform can lead. I'll pair with devx on schema.

sara: I'll draft the migration checklist (backwards compat, token metadata, server defaults).

natalie: I'll own docs.

alex: Great — I'll open the RFC patch referencing this thread and include the proposed json schema and example client flow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
